of them and FALSE of a sixth, which already does exactly the right thing:

    endless task unsettled --all

    … 64 more rows (--no-limit)

    --limit INTEGER    Max rows to render (default: 20; --no-limit for all).
    --no-limit         Render every row, however many there are.

So the default cap, the footer, and the escape flag are all already built and
shipped there. Measured 2026-08-28: `task unsettled` has them; `task list`,
`task recent`, `task active`, `task next` and `task search` have no limit flag at
all.

Two consequences for whoever picks this up:

1. **The spelling is already decided.** My recommendation above suggested
   `--limit 0` or `--all` for "no cap" — IGNORE THAT. `task unsettled` uses
   `--limit N` plus a separate `--no-limit`, and a second spelling for the same
   idea would be worse than the inconsistency this task exists to fix. Follow the
   existing one.
2. **The work is propagation, not design.** Lift whatever renders that footer out
   of the unsettled path and apply it to the surfaces that lack it. That also
   makes the machine-format question above easier to settle: check what
   `task unsettled` already does for `--json` and match it, or if it does nothing
   there, that gap is the only genuinely new design in this task.

Note `--all` on `task unsettled` means "survey every worktree" (which rows to
consider), NOT "show every row" (how many to render). Two different axes that
read alike; do not collapse them.



## Flag spelling, settled 2026-08-28 by Mike

Ship BOTH spellings as synonyms:

    --limit 0      terse, for agents
    --no-limit     legible, for humans

`--limit 0` alone was judged cryptic; `--no-limit` alone loses the terse form.
They are the same switch, so implement one and alias the other rather than
carrying two code paths.

`--all` is NOT in play and must not be recruited for this. It already means a
different axis on the surfaces that have it — WHICH ROWS to consider, not HOW
MANY to render: `task list --all` includes terminal statuses, `task unsettled
--all` surveys every worktree rather than one. Overloading it to also mean "no
cap" would collide on exactly the commands that need both at once.

## From the description

Which commands need it is for the implementor to determine and confirm with the user.

fields.title: Make the worktree-removal prohibition categorical
fields.description: Make worktree removal categorically forbidden in the handoff templates, with no precondition for a session to mis-evaluate, while keeping ask-first for worktree land.
fields.context:
Every spawned session's handoff says "Don't run 'endless worktree land'/'drop' without asking."

That form makes the session evaluate a precondition — have I been asked? — and that evaluation is where it fails: on 2026-08-25 two sessions destroyed worktrees within ten minutes, neither overriding the rule, both concluding the precondition was met by conversational text that did not meet it. One caused real damage.
fields.analysis: Six handoff templates carry the line, and the rule must name the outcome (drop, reap, git worktree remove) rather than one command, since a drop-only prohibition is satisfiable by another route.

fields.title: Remove background agents and deprecated sessions columns
fields.description: Remove all background-agent support and drop four deprecated sessions columns in one migration, clearing the sessions table's deprecation debt.
fields.notes: Blocks E-2063, which would otherwise classify each column when it splits sessions into session_instances.
fields.context: Background agents never became as reliable as tmux-hosted sessions; E-1695 routed the handoff template away from them on 2026-06-30 as a TEMPORARY measure and nothing reversed it in the two months since, so the code goes rather than keep being carried.
fields.analysis:
Delete all background-agent support — `task spawn --bg`/`--attach`, `task attach`, `endless agents`, `session-query record-bg-agent`, `spawn-window --attach`, monitor.RecordBgAgentSession/DecorateBgSession/ListBgAgents, bg_agents.go, the sessionkind package and the session_kinds table.

Then drop the four columns: short_id and kind_id (served only background agents), summary (superseded by the on-demand recap of E-1925), and plan_file_path (E-1338, which proposed a home-relative prefix for it, is declined, and its Set/GetPlanFilePath path is vestigial).

fields.title: Cap the session listings with a self-announcing footer
fields.description: Cap session list, search, history and trail with the same self-announcing row cap the task listings have, so a full page is distinguishable from a truncated one.
fields.context:
E-2071 gave nine task/decision/epic surfaces a shared row cap that announces what it dropped (src/endless/rowcap.py, '… N more rows (--no-limit)'). Its scope deliberately stopped short of the session listings, which still carry the original defect:

`session list`, `session search` and `session history` each cap at a silent --limit 20 and `session trail` at 50, with no footer — a result of exactly 20 is indistinguishable from a truncated one, which is the failure mode E-2071 was filed against.
fields.analysis:
`jobs list`, `verb list`, `phrase list`, `worktree list` and `project list` are uncapped and should be audited in the same pass.

The mechanism already exists and is tested; this is adoption, not design: thread rowcap.limit_options through each command, resolve with machine=as_json, and echo_footer after the render.

session trail and session search read through Go (session-query), so those two need the cap applied on the Python render side or a matching footer in the Go renderer — that is the only open question.

fields.title: Move per-task verify scripts out of tests/
fields.description: Move per-task verify scripts out of the tests directory so they no longer look like a test suite a glob can sweep up, making running another task's script structurally hard.
fields.context:
Per-task verify scripts live in tests/tasks/*.sh, which makes them look like a test suite.

They are not one: each drives real binaries (hook, endless-go, git, tmux) and several are not isolated from the live environment.

Running e-1202-verify writes a session row into the MAIN database bound to the caller's actual tmux pane, after which two sessions claim one pane and every companion-resolving command, esu included, refuses to pick between them.
fields.analysis:
## Why relocation, not just a stronger rule

The rule already exists and has been violated repeatedly. What makes it fragile
is that the scripts are shelved with a real test suite: `just test` runs
tests/, the scripts sit at tests/tasks/, and "check for regressions" reads as
"run what is under tests/". Nothing about the path says "these execute against
live state, one at a time, by the session that owns the task".

## What is actually unsafe

Relocation stops accidental sweeps. It does not stop a deliberate wrong run,
and it does not make the scripts safe. The underlying hazard is that some of
them reach the live environment at all:

- e-1202-verify pipes a synthetic payload into the real hook binary with no
  --config-dir and no XDG_CONFIG_HOME override, so the hook lazy-creates a
  session row in the main database and binds it to $TMUX_PANE.
- Others shell out to git, tmux and endless-go; how many are hermetic is
  unknown and worth measuring rather than assuming.

Newer scripts (e-2067, e-2071) build a throwaway config dir under the cache
sandbox root and run the CLI from outside the repo, so the pattern for a
hermetic fixture already exists in-tree and can be the model.

## Scope to settle before moving anything

- Where they land. `.verify/` keeps them near .endless/ and out of tests/;
  a sibling of tests/ that is not tests/ is the only hard requirement.
- Every reference that resolves a script by task id: the justfile, docs/guide,
  `endless verify`, the scripts' own "Run from inside the worktree" headers,
  and any spawn/handoff prose that names the path.
- Whether a guard belongs in the harness — refusing a bulk invocation outright
  beats relying on the reader to notice the directory changed.
- An audit of which scripts touch live state, and whether those should be made
  hermetic on the same pass or tracked separately.

## From the description

The rule is that a session runs its OWN task's script and no other; the layout works against it, because any glob over tests/ sweeps them in.

fields.title: Make the companion resolver compare full pane identity
fields.description: Make the companion resolver compare pane identity as the writer records it, or order by last activity, instead of refusing when sessions on different pane processes share an address.
fields.notes: The read half never landed.
fields.context:
E-1898 replaced pane identity with (server_uuid, address) and removed TouchSession's collision invalidation on the reasoning that a reissued pane resolves to a DIFFERENT processes row, so "the case cannot arise" — and that a genuine same-server collision "leaves both rows alone and readers order by last_activity".

Reproduced: sessions 976 (process_id 91, last active 2026-08-06) and 1152 (process_id 185) both read as %422, which blocked esu in that tmux window.

Neither row is wrong — they are two different panes that share an address string.

fields.title: Merge project verbs with the built-in defaults
fields.description: Merge verb sources instead of using the first one that exists, so a project's verbs.jsonl, even a one-entry auto-registered one, no longer shadows all the built-in default verbs.
fields.context:
Auto-registration writes newly-seen lead verbs into the project's .endless/verbs.jsonl with no completable flag, so on a fresh project the first unknown verb creates a one-entry file that shadows all 18 completable defaults.

E-1240's gate then refuses 'completed' for every audit/research title, with a message that names the wrong cause.

fields.title: Investigate how a session can get its spawn handoff
fields.description: Investigate whether a command renders the spawn handoff on demand for a session that started without one, and if not, recommend how a running session should obtain it.
fields.context: endless task spawn generates a handoff and passes it to the Claude session it opens, but a session started any other way — or one whose harness instance was re-minted by a clear — never receives that text and has no known way to ask for it.

fields.title: Drop the session-navigation trail
fields.description: Drop the session-navigation trail: its tables and the session trail command.

fields.title: Research artifact-write and DB-context paths after Go port
fields.description: Research, against the ported Go code, the map of non-ledger file writers and the DB-context resolution that the earlier ledger-routing research said would expire with the port.
fields.notes:
## Justification

Mike asked for a cleans-up research task so E-1732 can close per ED-1550. The deliverable is a factual map that E-1665, E-1730 and E-2035 all read before they can be planned; no single do-task owns it, and inlining it would duplicate it three times.

## From the description

E-894 and its siblings under E-1486 rewrite exactly those call sites.

Recorded for accuracy: E-1732's outcome was never read or accepted — it was closed because ED-1550 forbids reopening shipped work to extend it.
fields.context: E-1732 mapped ledger-target routing on 2026-08-27 and landed (d4a5ff0), but two of its nine sections expire with the Go port and say so in the outcome: section 1's table of non-ledger file writers, and section 3's Python half of DB-context resolution.
fields.analysis: Treat it as unreviewed source material.

fields.title: Restore four deleted verify suites and revert eight amended
fields.description: Restore from git history the four landed verify suites deleted by the background-agent removal and revert its amendments to eight others, since landed verify suites must not be edited.
fields.notes: E-2074 deleted four landed verify suites for the features it removed and amended eight more where they asserted on what it took out, with its own suite asserting the four are gone.
fields.context: Mike, on being shown this during E-2081: E-2074 BADLY VIOLATED the principles of Endless.
fields.analysis:
Deleted by E-2074 (commit bf285b54): the e-1568, e-1570, e-1572 and e-1621 verify suites. Amended by the same commit: e-1573, e-1624, e-1645, e-1648, e-1659, e-1905, e-1906, e-1914, e-1967 and e-2067. Its rationale was 'a suite that proves a deleted feature works is worse than no suite'.

The guide's answer to that concern is different and already written: leave the suite alone, let it fail, and move coverage that must survive into the durable suite (just test, go test). A landed suite is a record, not a regression test, so a stale one costs nothing — nothing under tests/tasks/ is imported, executed at build time, or read by the product.

Restoring the four is a straight git revert of those paths. The twelve amendments need reading one at a time: some are pure retrofits to keep a suite green and revert cleanly, but E-2074's own message claims three of them (e-1573, e-1914, e-2067) fixed real pre-existing leftovers its sweep caught — decide per file whether the restored text is the honest historical record or was already wrong when it landed.

Then E-2074's own verify script needs its assert_absent block on the four deleted paths replaced, since after this they exist again.

The violation propagated before it was caught: E-2081, working the same kind of removal three days later, read E-2074 as the convention and deleted E-1682's suite, amended e-2071 and e-2037, and ran both. All of that was reverted. E-1916 (block edits and runs of landed suites from the PreToolUse hook) would have refused every one of those moves at the tool call and is still only submitted; until it lands, the rule is prose an agent can rationalise past — and this is twice now that one did.

## From the description

That inverts the rule: a landed verify suite is a one-shot land-time gate whose post-land pass/fail is undefined, and it must not be edited because it records what was true when its task landed — deleting one being the strongest possible edit.

fields.title: Review what must land or move before the Go port
fields.description: Review which open tasks and which unsettled worktrees must land before the Go port starts, proposing a blocker list, landing order and any re-parents for approval.
fields.context: Two questions must be answered before E-1063 can start, and neither yields to a keyword search.
fields.analysis:
## Already done, do not redo

- E-1063 is type `epic` (it was `todo`).
- E-1486, E-894 and this task are its direct children. The tree is deliberately
  FLAT: nested tasks make it hard to see what needs doing, so add depth only
  with a reason worth stating.

## Measured 2026-08-28

- 136 worktrees on disk under `.endless/worktrees`.
- 84 of them unsettled. `endless task unsettled --all` is the survey command and
  it paginates at 20, so pass `--no-limit`.
- Some carry very large unlanded counts: E-1844 at 223 commits, E-1785 at 198,
  E-1853 at 182, E-1829 and E-1834 at 11 each. A high count usually means the
  branch is far behind main rather than that it contains that much work; check
  before treating it as a large change.
- One row reads `(no task row)` — E-1279. A worktree whose task is gone is its
  own small decision.
- 57 open tasks match a Go-or-Python keyword sweep. Treat that as a candidate
  pool to triage, NOT as an answer. Most will be incidental mentions.

## Question 1 is mostly about ORDER, not ownership

The expected outcome is a set of `blocked_by` edges on E-1063, not a pile of new
children. Three buckets, and most candidates land in the third:

- BLOCKER — the port would clobber this work, or this work must exist first.
  Record as `endless task block E-1063 --by <id>`.
- CHILD — this IS part of moving the surface to Go. Expected to be a short list.
- NEITHER — mentions Python or Go incidentally. Leave it exactly where it is.

A fourth bucket worth calling out if you find it: tasks the port SUBSUMES, which
stop existing once Go owns the surface. Those are obsolete-on-land candidates,
not blockers — flag them, do not close them.

## Question 2 method note

The risk is not "unlanded work exists". It is "unlanded work that touches Python
the port will delete". A worktree editing only Go, docs or tests is cheap to land
after the port; one rewriting `src/endless/task_cmd.py` is not. Sort by what the
branch touches, not by how long it has sat.

Also worth checking: whether a worktree branched before E-1891 can still run
`endless` at all. That landing broke worktrees whose stale `endless-go` predated
the status registry, because `cli.py` imports the registry at module level ahead
of the re-exec that would route around it. A worktree that cannot run the CLI
cannot easily be landed by its own session.

## From the description

A few may genuinely belong UNDER E-1063; treat that as the smaller, secondary finding.

Deliver a proposed blocker list, a proposed landing order, and any proposed re-parents, each entry with a one-line reason, for Mike to approve before anything is moved or landed.

fields.title: Install the tmux integration from endless setup
fields.description: Install the tmux integration from endless setup, writing the tmux config line that triggers it, so it survives tmux server restarts without a manual apply.
fields.context:
'endless setup' has no tmux subcommand and setup.py contains zero tmux references, so the tmux-conf line that 'endless tmux init' documents as its own trigger is never written — making init unreachable for anyone who has not hand-edited their tmux config. The only working path is running 'endless tmux apply' by hand, which is ephemeral and must be repeated after every tmux server restart, and the reference guide documents apply without ever mentioning init or the conf line.

So a PRODUCT user gets no second status row, no popup menus, and no way to make either persist.

fields.title: Fix task unsettled counting rebased commits as unlanded
fields.description: Fix task unsettled and the session-status marker to compare commits by patch-id, so commits landed rebased onto main no longer count as unlanded.
fields.context:
endless task unsettled --all reports 86 unsettled worktrees; git cherry (patch-id) over the same population gives 14.

E-1934 reports 314 unlanded commits and holds 2; E-1844 reports 223 and holds 4.
fields.analysis:
## Evidence (measured 2026-08-30)

`endless task unsettled --all` reported 86 unsettled worktrees. Re-running the
same population through `git cherry main <branch>` — which matches by patch-id
rather than SHA — gives 14 branches holding any commit not already on main.

Worst offenders, reported vs. actual:

| Branch | `unsettled` says | `git cherry` says |
|---|---|---|
| E-1934 | 314 | 2 |
| E-1844 | 223 | 4 |
| E-1785 | 198 | 2 |
| E-1853 | 182 | 6 |
| E-1537 | 122 | 2 |

## Cause

`worktree land` rebases the branch before fast-forwarding main. The rebase
rewrites SHAs, so main receives a copy of each commit under a new hash while
the branch retains the original. Any check based on "is this SHA reachable from
main" reports the branch's copies as unlanded permanently, and the number grows
with every subsequent land on the branch.

## Why it matters

The count is the input to every "what is outstanding?" judgement. At ~6× it
makes a 14-branch backlog look like an 86-branch one, and it buries the handful
of branches that genuinely hold work under a pile that does not. It also makes
the number grow over time for branches that are *more* settled, not less.

## Scope

Replace the SHA-reachability check with a patch-id comparison (`git cherry`, or
`git log --cherry-mark --left-right`) in whatever `unsettled` and the `session
status` ◆ probe share — the two read the same probe by design and must keep
doing so.

Note the separate case the fix should keep visible: a branch can carry patches
that are genuinely absent from main and still be undesirable to land, because
main has moved past them by another route. Four branches here (E-1537, E-1785,
E-1844, E-1934) hold only a README rewrite that E-1832 superseded. Patch-id
correctly calls those unlanded; it is the operator who has to decide they are
not worth landing. That is out of scope here — just do not paper over it.



## Correction from E-2089: patch-id is not sufficient — use `git range-diff`

E-2089 re-measured this population and found the prescribed fix falls short.
Patch-id survives a plain rebase, but `worktree land` rebases onto a moving main
and conflict resolution CHANGES the diff — after which the branch copy and the
landed copy have different patch-ids and read as unlanded forever. The four
README branches named above are exactly that case, and the earlier reading of
them as "genuinely absent from main" was wrong:

- `98bb7b24` landed as `785fe07b`; `4e611073` landed as `a8bfccff`. Same
  subjects, different SHAs AND different patch-ids. E-1832 is `confirmed` and
  its README rewrite is on main.
- `git cherry` still reports both as `+` on E-1803, E-1864, E-1865 and E-1929,
  which is the false positive this task exists to remove.

`git range-diff` pairs two commit series by content SIMILARITY rather than exact
patch-id, so a conflict-resolved commit is still matched to its landed
counterpart. Measured over every branch in this repo:

```
B=$(git merge-base main "$BR")
git range-diff "$B..$BR" "$B..main" | grep -E '^ *[0-9]+: +[0-9a-f]+ +< +-:'
```

Each matching row is a branch commit with NO counterpart on main. It clears
E-1803/1864/1865/1929 to zero unmatched, and still flags E-1115, E-1523 and
E-2010 — the branches that really did hold work main lacked. Drop rows whose
commit touches only `.endless/` and what remains is real unlanded work. Cost is
~1.5s on the worst branch here (320 commits against main's 1238), so it is fine
per-task and acceptable for an `--all` sweep.

## Two other readers want this same probe

Keep it one implementation, not three:

- **E-2095 part 2**, the not-on-main report, needs exactly "does this branch hold
  any commit main lacks?".
- **The reaper.** It is gated on `task_landings` — its comment says it "only
  touches dirs whose task has landed at least once" — so a worktree whose branch
  sits at main with nothing to land is settled and disposable but has no landing
  row and is never reclaimed. E-1360 and E-1697 are live examples: E-2084 reset
  both branches to main and both are still on disk holding nothing. The tempting
  shortcut is to record a landing so they reap; that writes a falsehood into the
  exact table the not-on-main report reads. The fix is to let the reaper accept
  "settled with nothing to land" alongside "landed", same TTL, same live-session
  refusal.

## From the description

Switch the probe that unsettled and the session-status marker share to a patch-id comparison.

fields.title: Build the self_dev land-time migration-only executable
fields.description: Build a migration-only executable, compiled from the landing branch and carrying only its migrations, that worktree land runs to apply a self_dev land's migrations, since neither other binary may.
fields.context: ED-1567 forbids a CANDIDATE binary from migrating the real ledger, but `_resolve_land_endless_go` hands a self_dev land the worktree's own binary — a candidate — and E-1664 made that an invariant, since it is the only binary whose embedded schema and enums match the rows the land just wrote.
fields.analysis:
It runs migrations in full (DDL plus their DML) and never serves a hook or touches business data, which is what makes it immune to the binary-expects-a-schema failure.

self_dev only.

fields.title: Investigate terminal tasks whose code never landed
fields.description: Investigate tasks recorded confirmed, assumed or completed whose code is not on main, finding for each how it reached a terminal status without landing, and grouping the causes.
fields.context: Task status is therefore not a reliable answer to 'is this on main?', which is the question anyone planning work actually asks.
fields.analysis:
Deliverable is findings: which tasks are affected, and for each, how it reached a terminal status without landing.

Group the causes.

Propose fixes in the outcome for discussion; do not implement them.

Count the affected tasks at the time of the work — any number written here would be stale.

fields.title: Record sessions paused on a permission prompt
fields.description: Record a session paused on a permission prompt as waiting on the user, using Claude Code's notification hook, instead of letting it read as 'working'.
fields.notes: E-1976 built the display side and left the producer out: its board's first rank has none.
fields.analysis:
## What is missing

Endless installs six Claude Code hooks — PreToolUse, SessionStart,
UserPromptSubmit, PostToolUse, Stop, SessionEnd. None reports that Claude Code is
asking the user for permission, so a session sitting on a prompt reads `working`,
indistinguishable from one doing work. `Notification` is the event that reports
it and was never wired.

E-1976 built the display side and left the producer out: `actWaiting` is the
board's first rank, wears the warning glyph, renders bold, and `classify()`
already routes a state to it. The rank has no producer. That is this task.

## What "waiting on the user" means here

Decided with Mike (2026-09-03): a session is waiting on the user whenever it has
paused for input, whether or not it asked a question. A finished turn and a
question are the same thing for this purpose — the ball is in the user's court —
which is exactly what his tmux window flag already signals and has proven
accurate in practice.

That definition is what keeps the task small. There is no question-versus-
finished classification, no inspection of the turn's final message, and no model
call. `idle` already means "the turn ended", so the work is to add the one
paused-for-input case Endless cannot currently see — a permission prompt — and to
make the vocabulary say that both are the same kind of waiting.

Explicitly not coupled to the minimizer. It is disabled until further notice,
will be renamed when it returns, and nothing on this task's critical path may
depend on it.

## What the current hooks reference says

Checked against the live documentation rather than recall, which was two months
and twenty-four events out of date.

Claude Code exposes 33 hook events. `Notification` carries a `notification_type`
field whose documented values include `permission_prompt` and `idle_prompt`.

Two findings that shaped the design:

- `agent_needs_input` exists but is scoped to agent-team teammates about to go
  idle, alongside a `TeammateIdle` event. It is NOT a main-session "the agent
  asked you something" signal, and designing on it would have been wrong.
- `PermissionRequest` is now a first-class event carrying `tool_name`,
  `tool_input` and `tool_use_id`. It is nevertheless the wrong signal for this
  task: it fires whenever a permission DECISION is needed, which an allowlist or
  another hook can resolve without the user ever seeing anything.
  `Notification` with `permission_prompt` fires when the user is actually
  prompted, which is the fact this task records.

## Why a new state rather than `needs_input`

`needs_input` looks like the obvious home and is not. It is ENFORCED:
`hookcmd.sessionMayWrite` refuses file writes from a session in that state under
`enforce` tracking, with the message "you asked your user something and the
answer has not arrived. There is no command for you to run."

That state means the AGENT asked the USER something. A permission prompt is the
reverse — the agent is trying to act and the harness is asking — and routing one
to the other would refuse the session's next write after the user approved.

The near miss is worth recording because it was not carelessness. The gate's
admission set was a Go `switch` with a silent `default: return false`, so a new
state joined the refused set without anyone deciding it should. That is why
E-2105 came first: with `MayWrite` a named group, a state cannot be added
without the question being answered.

## Why `prompted` may write

Decided with Mike (2026-09-01), from the gate's own stated rule rather than from
preference. The gate admits a session that "has DECLARED what it is working on
and is live-and-acting", and already glosses `idle` as admissible because "a
write from an idle session is by definition mid-turn". A prompt-blocked session
is mid-turn by exactly that reasoning, and the tool it waits on is its own.

The decisive argument was the asymmetry of failure modes. Both readings need a
clearing transition. If the clear misses under this one, a stale glyph sits on
the board until the next Stop — cosmetic, self-correcting. If it missed under the
other, every prompted session would be refused its next write and told there is
no command to run, which is the failure E-2093 was cleaning up after.

## The `needs_input` writers are the real defect underneath

Two writers put `needs_input` in the database and neither means a person is being
waited on: `monitor.InitSession` writes it as a row's initial value at
SessionStart, and the revive-an-ended-row CASE writes it on any incoming hook
(E-1686). Nothing else writes it.

Measured while E-1976 was built: 34 rows in `endless` carrying it, every one last
active 25 to 71 days earlier, none on a pane that still existed — sessions that
registered and never had a turn.

E-1976 responded by excluding the state from the board. Mike's correction
(2026-09-03): that is backwards. Hiding them is how they rotted unseen, the board
already caps each rank at ten rows with a footer naming the remainder — machinery
built for exactly this — and revealing them is what provides the mechanism to
resolve them.

So this task reveals the rows and fixes the writers, and deliberately does not
retire the existing 34. They are surfaced to be dealt with, not migrated away in
the dark. Once drained, `needs_input` has no writer and no rows, and means only
what the declaration gate says it means.

## From the description

Install the hook, add a 'prompted' state to internal/sessionstate classified into all five groups (MayWrite included, so approving a prompt never leaves the session refused), route notification_type permission_prompt to it and idle_prompt to idle, and clear it on the session's next activity.

Waiting on the user means the session paused for input, question or not, so AwaitsHuman becomes the one place that answers it.

Also stops InitSession and the revive CASE from writing needs_input, and reveals those rows on the board instead of hiding them.

fields.title: Export the suite directory to verify.toml checks
fields.description: Export the suite directory to verify.toml checks, as verify.sh suites already get it, so a check can reference its own files without hand-writing the path.
fields.context:
A verify.sh suite gets ENDLESS_VERIFY_RUN/TAP/TASK from the runner; a verify.toml [[check]] gets nothing, so a check needing a file from its own suite directory retypes the path.

.endless/tasks/e-1603/verify.toml does: command = "sh .endless/tasks/E-1603/e2e.sh" — uppercase, where the tracked directory is e-1603. It runs only because APFS is case-insensitive; on any case-sensitive filesystem that check cannot find its own script.

fields.title: Fix idle-session lockout and missing suite path in handoff
fields.description: Fix two gaps: mark an idle session working again when its next turn starts so the write gate stops blocking it, and have the handoff say where a verify suite goes and that it must source the harness.
fields.context:
Two unrelated gaps, folded to hold the backlog.

The PreToolUse gate admits only state='working', so a session that completes one clean turn can never Write again; other states fall into a branch announcing 'No active work session', false for an idle session that holds a task. The refusal names `task claim`, which refuses on status first, and --force clears that only by demoting the task.

Both observed sessions finished through Bash heredocs.

Reporting 'unverified' is not the trigger, only what a session does last.

fields.title: Canonicalize the verify runner's temp HOME
fields.description: Canonicalize the temp HOME the verify runner gives each suite, resolving macOS's symlinked temp root, so suites stop failing for reasons unrelated to their task.
fields.notes: Repointed: the test is not where this belongs.
fields.context:
E-2023's runner hands every suite a temp HOME from os.MkdirTemp, and on macOS the OS temp root sits beneath a symlinked prefix (var -> private/var) — so every suite runs under a HOME reached through a symlink, which a real home directory almost never is.

That is an artifact of the isolation MECHANISM, not a property of the code under test; it is platform-dependent (passes on Linux, fails on macOS); and it makes suites fail for reasons unrelated to their own task, which is the one thing a verification front door must never do.

The whole internal/monitor package then passes under a temp HOME, so the planned per-test fix and the sweep for other HOME-sensitive tests both become unnecessary.
fields.analysis:
Repointed 2026-08-31 by ES-1159 (E-2023), at Mike's direction, after he asked
whether E-2023 could have been implemented so that this task were unnecessary.
It could — and the answer moves the fix from the test to the runner.

## What was originally filed, and why it was the wrong layer

`TestProjectPath_TildeExpandsToHome` (internal/monitor/projects_test.go) builds
its expectation as `filepath.Join(os.UserHomeDir(), "some-project")` and
compares it against `ProjectPath`, which returns the RESOLVED form. The two
agree only when HOME is not itself reached through a symlink. The original plan
was to fix the expectation and sweep for the same shape elsewhere.

The test IS wrong — it compares a resolved value against an unresolved one. But
nothing had ever observed it, and after the change below nothing will again.
Under ED-1550, "noticing something true does not earn a task."

## Where it actually belongs

`makeRunDir` (internal/verifycmd/env.go) takes `os.MkdirTemp("")` verbatim. On
macOS that lands beneath a symlinked prefix, so the runner hands every suite a
HOME reached through a symlink — something a real home directory almost never
is.

Three reasons that is the runner's bug and not the test's:

1. It is an artifact of the isolation MECHANISM, not a property of the system
   under test. The runner's job is to substitute HOME transparently; anything
   else it changes is noise it injected.
2. It is platform-dependent. The same suite, the same code, passes on Linux
   (the temp root is not symlinked there) and fails on macOS. A runner whose
   verdict depends on the OS's mktemp implementation emits false signal.
3. It misattributes failures — this task's own sharpest observation, that "the
   failure it reports will point at the wrong task." That is precisely the harm
   E-2023 exists to prevent.

The counter-argument from E-2023's plan — "a break is a finding, not a
regression" — was written about suites that secretly depended on the real
database, where the dependency was always a contract violation. It does not
transfer. Nothing in the contract says a suite must tolerate a symlinked HOME,
and the runner is not a fuzzer; a deliberate test of symlinked-HOME behaviour is
a thing someone can write on purpose.

## The change

`filepath.EvalSymlinks` on the freshly created temp dir, failing open (a
directory this process just made should always resolve; if it does not, running
under the unresolved path beats refusing to verify).

Measured before and after:

    raw temp HOME       -> FAIL  ProjectPath = "<resolved>" want "<unresolved>"
    resolved temp HOME  -> ok    internal/monitor

The whole `internal/monitor` package passes under a resolved temp HOME, with
that test the only failure under the raw one — so the sweep this task planned
finds nothing left to fix.

## Pinned, not left to the platform

Three tests, because the invariant is invisible on Linux and would rot silently:

- `TestMakeRunDir_IsCanonical` — the run dir equals its EvalSymlinks form.
- `TestIsolatedEnv_HomeIsCanonical` — HOME and XDG_CONFIG_HOME, the values
  consumers actually see, are canonical.
- `TestRun_ScriptSuite_SeesCanonicalHome` — end to end through the real runner:
  a suite observing a non-canonical HOME exits 30 and fails the test.

## Verification of the original symptom, end to end

A throwaway suite driven through `endless-go verify`, whose check was the exact
repro from the original filing, printed a canonical HOME and passed. Before the
change it failed.

## PRODUCT

Nothing macOS-specific in the fix, though the symptom is. Any platform whose
temp root is symlinked hands the same trap to every downstream project's
suites, and the runner is shipped surface.

## From the description

Fix: canonicalize the run dir in makeRunDir with filepath.EvalSymlinks. One line.

fields.title: Surface landed and still-authoritative state for tasks
fields.description: Surface whether a task's work has actually landed and whether a task or decision record is still authoritative, since status is routinely read as answering both and answers neither.
fields.context:
Task status answers "what did we decide about this work".

It is routinely read as "has this code landed?" and "is this record still authoritative?", and it answers neither.

E-2089 measured the cost: E-1115 sat 'assumed' with its fix on an unlanded branch, so the same bug was found and fixed again 14 days later as E-1395; and thirteen tasks read 'confirmed'/'assumed' while the code they describe had been deleted from the base branch, with nothing recorded to say so until E-2089 added the relations by hand.
fields.analysis:
Task status answers "what did we decide about this work". It is routinely read as "is this code on main?" and "is this record still authoritative?", and it answers neither. E-2089 measured the cost: E-1115 sat `assumed` with its fix on an unlanded branch, so the same bug was found and fixed a second time 14 days later as E-1395; and thirteen tasks read `confirmed`/`assumed` while the code they describe had been deleted from main, with nothing recorded to say so until E-2089 added the relations by hand. The same gap has a decisions half — I have repeatedly quoted a task or decision as authoritative without noticing it was obsolete, declined, replaced, or not yet accepted.

Five parts, one problem: the reader cannot see the facts that decide whether to trust the row.

(1) `task show` must STATE landedness for a task in a terminal status rather than imply it by omission. Today the `Landed:` line appears only when a `task_landings` row exists, so "landed before landings were recorded" and "the branch is still sitting there" render identically — as nothing. Three cases, three sentences: `Landed: <ts> <sha>`; `Landed: never — created before landings were recorded (pre 2026-04-22)`; `Landed: never — branch <b> holds N commits not on main`.

(2) Add a "not on main" report — the join nothing does today. Tasks in a terminal status, created on or after the first landing record (2026-04-22), with no landing row OR with a branch holding source commits main lacks. The core is one git call per branch and needs no judgement: `B=$(git merge-base main $BR); git range-diff $B..$BR $B..main`, counting rows whose left side is a commit and right side is `-:`. Drop commits touching only `.endless/`. Use `git range-diff`, NOT `git cherry` — E-2087 asks for a patch-id check, and patch-id is exactly what breaks: `worktree land` rebases, conflict resolution changes the diff, and the branch copy then reads as unlanded forever. Measured on this repo, range-diff clears all four known false-positive branches to zero and still flags E-1115, E-1523 and E-2010; worst case ~1.5s on a 320-commit branch. Mike's framing: this belongs in project status (E-1976), not only in a command run by hand.

(3) Make an excision record what it excises. When a task deletes files another task's landed commits created, emit (or prompt for) the `replaced_by` edge — as E-1449 did by hand for the plan-snapshot deletion and as E-1939, E-2029, E-2074, E-2081, E-1426 and E-1711 did not. `endless task replace <old> --by <new>` already does the right thing once called, including holding shipped work at the status it earned; the gap is that nothing calls it. NOTE: this part needs a recording change first. `task_landings` stores a merge SHA but no base, so the landed commit range cannot be reconstructed, and `task_files` stopped recording 2026-07-11. Persist the landed file set (or the base SHA) at land time and the join becomes exact.

(4) Lead `task show`, `decision show` and their siblings with an IMPORTANT banner when the record is not straightforwardly authoritative: task is obsolete/declined/replaced_by, decision is not yet accepted or has been rejected/superseded. The status line is already on screen and is demonstrably not enough — it is read as provenance, not as a caveat. The banner states the caveat before the content it qualifies.

(5) Say it in the guide, next to (1)'s rendering: a task status answers "what did we decide about this work", never "where is the code".

Scope note: parts 1, 2, 4 and 5 are implementable now. Part 3 is blocked on the recording change named in it; if that makes this task too large, split part 3 out rather than dropping the recording change.

## From the description

Details in --analysis.

fields.title: Fix Write/Edit block after a bash-input turn start
fields.description: Fix the write gate blocking every Write and Edit for the rest of a turn started with Claude Code's bash input, by marking the session working even though no prompt was submitted.
fields.context:
A turn started with Claude Code's `!` bash-input fires no UserPromptSubmit, so the session is still 'idle' from the previous turn's Stop.

No sanctioned verb recovers it, so the only ways out are to demote the task, send an ordinary prompt, or route around the gate.

Hit live during E-1661 on 2026-08-31.

fields.title: Show an agent's refusal verdict as first and last line
fields.description: Show a refusal's one-line verdict as both the first and last line when an agent is running, so it survives a truncating pipe; humans see the message unchanged.
fields.context: Measured on task add/update: five refusals across two verbs, one answered by shaving 34 characters off a title without ever reading the 107>100 the error stated twice, and one by writing a junk value to a live record to probe the validator.
fields.analysis:
Fix: when agent_env.present(), emit ONE dense verdict line as both the FIRST and LAST line of the refusal, with the existing guidance unchanged between them.

Identical lines, not split, so whichever end survives a truncation is sufficient on its own.

Humans see today's message unchanged - the duplication is agent-only by design.

fields.title: Surface worktree drift continuously
fields.description: Surface worktree drift where a session already looks, such as session status or worktree list, and give the worktree sync sweep a progress and completion signal.
fields.context:
`endless worktree sync` reports and closes worktree drift, but only when a person runs it.

Nothing surfaces that a worktree is behind, so a change to a file every task shares reaches main and reaches no working checkout until someone thinks to sweep — which is how 138 of 142 worktrees came to predate a guard they all depend on.

There is also no way to watch a sweep's progress or be told when the fleet is current.

fields.title: Explore discouraging one-shot state-change tasks
fields.description: Explore how to discourage filing tasks whose deliverable is a one-shot state change with no artifact, and what signal could catch them at creation.
fields.context:
E-2089 found four tasks (E-1102, E-1134, E-1186, E-1327) that reached a terminal status having produced no code, because they should never have been filed as implementation work at all: the deliverable was a one-shot state change with no artifact — edit a plan file, run one command, observe one thing once.

E-1658's verb gate already refuses two of the four shapes ('Review and decide...', 'Decide...') because the lead verb is an investigation verb on an action type.

It cannot see the other three: 'Update E-971 plan...', 'Re-emit E-1100 phase change...', 'Verify E-989 companion file...' are all led by legitimate action verbs and were accepted on a probe against a sandbox DB.
fields.analysis:
The verb is not what is wrong, so a gate on the verb cannot catch them.

Open question: what signal distinguishes a task with a durable deliverable from one whose whole content is 'do this once', and can it be checked at creation without an intelligence call?

fields.title: Extend the reaper to reclaim settled, never-landed worktrees
fields.description: Extend the worktree reaper to reclaim a worktree that is settled with nothing to land but has no landing record, with the same expiry and live-session refusal as landed ones.
fields.context:
The reaper is gated on task_landings — its own comment says it 'only touches dirs whose task has landed at least once'.

E-1360 and E-1697 are live examples — E-2084 reset both branches to main and both are still on disk holding nothing.
fields.analysis:
Interaction with E-2095 part 2: both this and the not-on-main report need the
same underlying probe — "does this branch hold any commit main lacks?" — and it
should be one implementation, not two. E-2089 established that the probe must use
`git range-diff` rather than `git cherry`, because `worktree land` rebases and
conflict resolution changes the patch-id, after which the branch copy reads as
unlanded forever. Whichever of the two lands first should own the probe.

Do not weaken the existing refusals. The reaper already declines a worktree with
a live session in it, and that stays. "Settled" here means the same thing
`task unsettled` means — no uncommitted changes, and nothing on the branch that
main does not already have — not merely "the task looks finished".

## From the description

Recording a landing to make them reap is the wrong lever: it writes a falsehood into the exact table E-2095's not-on-main report reads.

Fix it in the reaper instead: treat settled-with-nothing-to-land as reclaimable alongside landed, same TTL, same live-session refusal.

fields.title: Track the work of a resumed session
fields.description: Track the tasks a session had already touched, as a container task auto-created so that session could be resumed into a worktree.
Name both tmux windows Endless creates for a task, from spawn and from resume, by the task id alone, keeping the sandbox reaper's window-name check working.
fields.context: `task spawn` builds `<project>_<one-or-two-words>[E-NNNN]`, spending a narrow tab on words the user already knows; `session goto --resume` passes no -n at all, so tmux falls back to the command and every resumed window reads `claude`.
fields.analysis:
Not a one-liner: internal/sandboxcmd/reapguard.go reads window names to decide which DB sandboxes to SPARE, matching the bracketed `[E-NNNN]` form specifically — its comment calls that the user's own record that the task is still in play.

Renaming without moving that regex silently drops the protection and lets a sandbox be reaped while its window is open.

The regex must match the bare form and keep matching the bracketed one, since windows named before this lands stay open.

fields.title: Notify sessions when a decision's status changes
fields.description: Notify the sessions involved with a decision when its status changes, as they are already notified of task status changes.
fields.context:
tasks_notify_sessions (E-1917) fires on a task UPDATE and inserts one session_notices row per involved session, which the UserPromptSubmit drain renders as an FYI line.

The decisions table carries only decisions_updated_at — no fan-out.

So a session files a decision, the user accepts or rejects it minutes later, and the session never learns; it keeps answering as though the call is still open.

Seen directly: the session that filed this had two decisions adjudicated mid-conversation, was told neither, and went on to state one of their statuses from memory, wrongly.
fields.analysis:

fields.description: Give the session state vocabulary an owning Go package, replacing string literals scattered across Go, Python and SQL, as a pure refactor with identical behaviour.
fields.notes: Blocks E-2091, which adds a fifth state and must be a one-row change.
fields.context: Session state (working, idle, needs_input, ended) is spelled as string literals across ~70 non-test sites in Go, Python and SQL, with no owning package — the defect E-1891 fixed for task status, unfixed here.
fields.analysis:
## The defect

`sessions.state` carries four values — `working`, `idle`, `needs_input`, `ended`
— and nothing owns them. They are spelled as string literals across roughly 70
non-test sites in three languages: Go (`internal/monitor`, `internal/hookcmd`,
`internal/projectstatuscmd`), Python (`src/endless/cli.py`,
`src/endless/session_cmd.py`), and SQL embedded in both.

This is precisely the defect E-1891 fixed for task status, left unfixed here.
`src/endless/statuses.py` records what it cost there: status lived as bare
literals across ~20 sites in two languages, and twice — E-1648's `submitted`,
E-1845's `untriaged` — a status was added and a site was missed.

Measured distribution of the SQL predicates:

- `state != 'ended'` — 29 sites. By an order of magnitude the most common thing
  anyone asks about a session.
- `state = 'ended'` — 21 sites.
- single-state reads and writes — the remainder.

## What made it urgent

E-1976 added a project attention board whose loudest rank is "a session is
waiting on you". Building its follow-up (E-2091) I proposed routing Claude
Code's permission-prompt Notification to `needs_input`, on the evidence that no
live transition ever writes that state.

That was wrong in a way a grep does not reveal. `needs_input` is enforced:
`hookcmd.sessionMayWrite` refuses file writes from a session in that state under
`enforce` tracking, with the message "you asked your user something and the
answer has not arrived. There is no command for you to run." Routing permission
prompts there would have refused the session's next write after the user
approved.

The failure is structural, not a lapse of care. The gate's admission set is a Go
`switch` with a silent `default: return false`. A new state joins the refused set
by default and says nothing. Nothing in the code makes adding a state a decision
about whether it may write.

## Why groups, and why these five

Each of the five is a predicate already in the tree, not a speculation. `Live`
retires the 29-site majority. `MayWrite` is the one that pays for the exercise:
once the gate reads a named group, a state cannot be added without someone
classifying it, which is the forcing function that would have caught the
collision above. `AwaitsHuman` is the group the board's attention rank expresses,
and drawing it now is what keeps E-2091 to one row. `DisplayOrder` and `All`
carry `session list`'s sort and the vocabulary itself.

This follows `internal/taskstatus`'s governing property: adding a Group is one
row; adding a Status means revisiting every row.

## Why a transition table but no generated diagram

Session state has been stable where task status has not. Twelve session-related
schema change files exist and not one touches `state`'s value set — sessions have
churned through short ids, nullable session_id, active epic, kind, gates added
and dropped, transcript path dropped, recap columns dropped, and the four values
held throughout. The live database has exactly four distinct values ever written.
Task status gained three members over a comparable stretch.

The two are different kinds of vocabulary. Task status models a human approval
workflow, which keeps acquiring distinctions people find worth drawing; session
state models a process lifecycle written by hooks, bounded by what a harness can
report. Realistic growth is one member (E-2091's fifth), plausibly a second for
stall detection.

So `taskstatus`'s generated-mermaid machinery — the artifact, the regeneration
recipe, the drift check, the three-copy sync test — is not justified here. It
earns its keep against thirteen states with per-task-type edges people
misremember. Four hook-written states do not have that problem.

The transition TABLE is justified on different grounds: its `trigger` column
names which code performs each write. "What actually writes `needs_input`?" is
the question that produced the wrong proposal above, and it stays expensive at
four states or six, because it is a question about writers scattered across two
languages rather than about how many values exist.

## Decisions taken with Mike (2026-09-01)

1. Pure refactor. No state is added here; E-2091 adds the fifth. The verification
   gate is behaviour byte-identical before and after, which is the only cheap way
   to prove a 70-site conversion broke nothing.
2. Five groups: All, Live, MayWrite, AwaitsHuman, DisplayOrder.
3. Transition table as data plus a test. No generated artifact.
4. Python converts now, not at the all-Go port. If Python keeps its own copy,
   E-2091's fifth state is rejected by `--state`'s Click choice and renders as
   the unknown glyph — the exact missed-site incident this pattern exists to
   prevent, and it would defeat the point of doing this task first.

## From the description

Build internal/sessionstate as its counterpart: members, labels, glyphs, five curated groups (All, Live, MayWrite, AwaitsHuman, DisplayOrder), SQLList, and a transition table naming which code writes each state.

Expose it as 'endless-go session-state' and convert Python to a thin pass-through holding none of the vocabulary.

Pure refactor: no state is added and behaviour is byte-identical.

Also deletes the obsolete duplicate CREATE TABLE sessions in db.py, whose banned CHECK constraint is a fifth vocabulary site.

fields.title: Rename task branches to task/<id>
fields.description: Rename worktree branches to task/<id> with no title slug so a branch name is derivable from the id, renaming existing slug branches and retiring the recorded branch name on landings.
fields.notes: Implements ED-1587:
fields.analysis:
## Scope

Implements ED-1587. Three pieces, in order:

1. **Construction.** `src/endless/worktree_cmd.py` and `:1653` build
   `f"task/{task_id}-{slug}"`. Both become `f"task/{task_id}"`. Whatever
   computes the slug for this purpose goes with them if nothing else uses it.

2. **Migration of the ~139 existing branches.** They are local-only — no
   remote, no PRs, no CI — so `git branch -m task/<id>-<slug> task/<id>` is
   cheap and safe. Each has a live worktree checked out on it, so the rename
   must go through git (which updates the worktree's HEAD), never by editing
   refs. Decide and state whether this is a one-shot `db apply-change`-style
   step or a resolver that accepts both forms during a transition; a one-shot
   rename is simpler and this project has no other clones to coordinate with.
   Sessions are live in some of these worktrees, so the rename must not run
   under them unannounced — gate it the way the reaper gates on
   `WorktreeInUse`, or require it to be run deliberately.

3. **Retire `task_landings.branch`.** Once the name is derivable the column is
   redundant. Two consequences worth doing in the same pass, because they are
   the reason the decision was made:
   - E-1719's record-only landing recorded no branch, which is why
     `maybeReapWorktree` scans it as `sql.NullString`. That case disappears.
   - E-2087 added a git fallback (`git symbolic-ref --short HEAD`) so a
     worktree with no landing row could still have its branch deleted at reap
     time, plus a carve-out that deliberately does NOT apply the fallback to a
     NULL-branch landing row. Both go away: the reaper derives `task/<id>`
     from the task id it already has.

   The column also feeds `internal/monitor/session_notices.go` and the
   `task landed` surface; check every reader before dropping it, and prefer
   deriving over reading rather than leaving a second source of truth.

## Also update

- `ED-1167` — supersede it via `endless decision supersede`, not by editing it.
- The guide's worktree/branch prose, wherever it shows a slug branch name.
- Any test fixture that hardcodes a `task/<id>-<slug>` branch.

## Out of scope

A configurable branch pattern. ED-1587 rejects it explicitly and says why.

## From the description

Covers the two construction sites in worktree_cmd.py, renaming the ~139 existing local-only slug branches, and retiring task_landings.branch — which takes E-1719's NULL-branch carve-out and E-2087's git-fallback-for-the-branch-name with it.

fields.title: Explore an Endless session without Claude or tmux
fields.description: Explore what an Endless session is with no Claude agent and no tmux: map what breaks without each, and whether an agent-less run should still record a session.
fields.context: Endless assumes Claude and tmux so foundationally that the agent-less path is barely designed: claim --unattended claims a task and leaves sessions.task_id unset, so the work has no session record and no route back.
fields.analysis:
## Three flags, one candidate name

Two existing flags are in play, they control unrelated machinery, and BOTH are
candidates to be replaced by `--no-agent`. They cannot both take the name, and
deciding that is part of this brainstorm rather than a detail to settle later.

- `claim --unattended` (E-2093) governs BINDING. With it, a task is claimed and
  `sessions.task_id` is left unset, so the work has no session record. Its half
  of the old `claim --force` was "claim with no Claude session bound".
- `--no-session` (E-1444) is GLOBAL, accepted in any position, and governs
  ATTRIBUTION. It sets a module flag the event write layer reads, which
  downgrades `actor.kind` to system and NULLs the envelope's session id. It
  exists, in its own words, for callers with no Claude session to attribute to:
  plain shell, cron, scripts. It does NOT skip session resolution — run it from
  a Claude pane and the claim still binds normally.

## Why the name collides

If the answer to the central question is "a session record always exists, and
what varies is whether an agent drives it", then both flags are misnamed by the
same reasoning, because in both cases the absent thing is the agent.

But the third possibility is more interesting than renaming either: if an
agent-less claim mints a session record, then `--no-session` may not need a new
name because it may not need to exist. Its whole purpose is to have somewhere to
put attribution when there is no session to credit. Give it a session to credit
and events can be attributed to that row instead of downgraded to system, and
the flag collapses rather than being renamed.

So the ordering is: settle whether an agent-less claim mints a session; then see
how many of these two flags survive; then name what is left. Renaming first
would be churn, which is the same reason the rename does not lead this task.

## From the description

If a session record is the spine, then what is absent in that case is an AGENT, not a session — which argues the flag should be --no-agent and should still mint a session, and raises the question of what a non-Claude session row holds and how it starts and ends.

Expect a follow-up research task.

The --unattended rename rides along rather than landing first, since renaming a flag before deciding whether the concept survives is churn.

fields.title: Decide how to get the exact unlanded answer cheaply
fields.description: Decide how the worktree reaper can use the exact answer to whether a branch holds unlanded work without paying its cost on every tool call, as the display surfaces already do.
fields.notes: E-2087 made 'does this branch hold work the base lacks?' exact via git range-diff, then had to be reverted on the worktree reaper because the reaper runs on PreToolUse/PostToolUse and a ~90s sweep stopped the product.
fields.context: The display surfaces keep the exact answer; the reaper is back to the cheap SHA check and its known leak.
fields.analysis:
## The problem

"Does this branch hold work the base branch lacks?" has an exact answer and a
cheap answer, and they are not the same answer.

- **Exact** (E-2087, `unlandedCommits` in internal/monitor/worktree_unlanded.go):
  `git range-diff` between the branch and the base since their merge base.
  Recognises a commit a rebasing land re-hashed, and one whose diff changed when
  a conflict was resolved. Measured cost: ~1-2s per worktree, scaling with how
  far the branch has drifted from the base, NOT with what the branch holds. A
  worktree 2251 commits behind main costs 2.1s on its own.
- **Cheap** (`reapNothingToLand` in internal/monitor/reap_worktrees.go):
  `git rev-list --count HEAD ^base ^<recorded landing>...`. One call, ~5ms.
  Cannot see a landing that was not recorded, so it over-reports outstanding
  work — safe for a delete decision, wrong for a display.

## What happened, and why this is filed

E-2087 replaced the SHA check with the exact one everywhere the two shared a
probe — including the worktree reaper. `monitor.ReapWorktreesForProject` is
called from FIVE branches of internal/hookcmd/claude.go, among them PreToolUse
and PostToolUse, so the reaper sweeps every worktree before and after every tool
call in every session. At ~90s per sweep that stopped the product, not just
`task spawn`.

The hotfix reverted the reaper to the cheap check and left the exact one on the
display surfaces (◆ in `session status`, `task unsettled`), which probe one row
or a handful rather than 139. The debt it accepted: a worktree whose work landed
under rewritten SHAs with no `task_landings` row reads as holding work forever,
so its directory is never reclaimed. That is the leak E-1940 and E-2087 each
tried to close, reopened deliberately because a slow leak is survivable and a
90-second tool call is not.

## What to decide

How to have the exact answer without paying for it per tool call. Directions
worth weighing, not a menu to pick from:

1. **Cache the verdict, keyed on (branch tip OID, base tip OID).** Both are
   ~1ms to read, and the key self-invalidates when either ref moves. The
   question is where it lives (a table? a file under the worktree's .git?) and
   what happens after a land, which moves the base and invalidates every entry
   at once — the cold sweep is back to ~90s unless something warms it.
2. **Take the reaper off the hook path.** A destructive background sweep
   running before and after every tool call is questionable independent of what
   it costs. Debounce it, run it on a timer, or move it to session start/end.
   This may be the real fix, with caching a nice-to-have on top.
3. **Make the exact answer cheaper.** The cost is dominated by patch-ids for
   every commit the base gained since the fork. Measured alternatives:
   `git cherry` (patch-id only) is ~3x faster but misses conflict-resolved
   landings; pairing by subject + author date is ~35x faster but disagrees with
   range-diff in BOTH directions, so it is unsafe alone. A union or a two-stage
   filter may be exact enough and much cheaper.
4. **Stop needing it.** ED-1587 makes branch names derivable and retires
   `task_landings.branch`. If landings were also recorded reliably, the cheap
   check would rarely be wrong — E-2087 measured worktrees whose work is on main
   with no landing row at all, and that recording gap is arguably the real
   defect underneath both leaks.

## Constraints any answer has to respect

- The reaper's mistakes are not symmetric. Refusing to reap costs disk; reaping
  a worktree that still holds work destroys it. Whatever it consults must be
  wrong only in the safe direction, or be exact.
- ◆, `task unsettled` and the reaper are supposed to agree about what "landed"
  means. The hotfix broke that on purpose and it should not stay broken.
- Whatever runs on the hook path is paid before and after every tool call.
  Budget it in milliseconds.

## Measured, after the hotfix — the sweep is still not cheap

On this project (139 worktrees, 41 of them past the 14d TTL and therefore
reaching git) the reaper's git sequence costs **2.58s per sweep**, on
PreToolUse AND PostToolUse. Down from ~90s, but not free, and it is paid twice
per tool call.

Two findings worth starting from:

- **Roughly 60% of it is re-deriving a constant.** The sequence per candidate
  is five git calls: three of them are `monitor.DefaultBranch` resolving
  `origin/HEAD` → `init.defaultBranch` → `rev-parse --verify main`. That is a
  property of the REPOSITORY, and all 139 worktrees share one. It is memoized
  per directory in a `sync.Map`, which does nothing here because every hook
  invocation is a fresh process. Caching per repo — or persisting it — cuts the
  sweep to roughly 1s without touching the accuracy question at all.
- **E-2087's eligibility change roughly doubled the candidate set.** Dropping
  the task_landings requirement admits 20 more worktrees (22 → 41) past the TTL
  gate and into git. That is the intended behaviour — those are precisely the
  never-recorded worktrees that could not be reclaimed — but it means the hot
  path got more expensive in exchange for reclaiming more, and nobody priced
  that at the time.

Both point the same way as direction 2: a sweep this shape does not belong on
PreToolUse/PostToolUse regardless of how fast each candidate is made.

## Measured 2026-09-06 — the display surfaces are not "a handful" either

The hotfix rationale above rests on a premise worth correcting: that leaving
the exact probe on the display surfaces was affordable because they "probe one
row or a handful rather than 139". On this machine they do not.

`session monitor` is a long-running view that re-probes every row it renders
every two seconds, and it is normal to have many panes open. Measured with the
reaper already off the exact probe:

- **13 concurrent `endless session monitor` processes**, uptimes 7 to 54
  minutes.
- Sampling `ps` once a second for ten seconds found **4-6 `git range-diff`
  processes in flight at every single instant** — never zero.

So the exact answer is a continuous multi-core background load, paid on the
DISPLAY path, with the reaper already excused from it. The cost model there is
(monitors x rows with worktrees x per-row range-diff), refreshed every two
seconds, with no cache — so every monitor pays again for work another monitor
just finished, and adding a pane multiplies the whole bill.

Three consequences for the directions above:

1. **Direction 1 (cache keyed on branch/base tip OIDs) is worth more than this
   analysis credits it.** It was weighed as a way to make the reaper's sweep
   affordable; it is also the only direction that fixes the display path, which
   is where the load actually is. Thirteen monitors sharing one cache pay for a
   worktree once per ref movement instead of 13 times per two seconds.

2. **The cold-sweep-after-a-land objection is worse on the display path than on
   the reaper's.** A land moves the base and invalidates every entry at once —
   and on the display path every monitor hits that cold cache simultaneously,
   within the same two-second tick.

3. **It is not only a cost problem.** With a range-diff always in flight, a
   Ctrl-C in any monitor pane kills one mid-run. The probe fails closed and
   records ERR-0010 against a task that is fine — observed for E-1972 at
   2026-09-06 00:20:03 EDT (`git range-diff: signal: interrupt`, one
   occurrence, while `task unsettled E-1972` answers cleanly on demand). The
   misclassification itself is filed as **E-2113** and is worth fixing whatever
   this task decides; it is noted here because the near-certainty of hitting it
   is a property of this cost problem, and a cheap or cached probe would shrink
   the window that makes it routine.

Per-worktree cost is confirmed in the range this analysis reports: e-1972 is
7 branch commits against the 648 main gained since its fork, and its
range-diff measures 0.9s. 128 worktrees are on disk.

## From the description

— caching keyed on branch/base tip OIDs, taking the reaper off the hook path, a cheaper exact algorithm, or fixing the landing-recording gap underneath.

fields.title: Fix session resume refusing to resume the pane's own task
fields.description: Fix session resume so resuming the task the pane already holds proceeds without --force, since it clobbers nothing, instead of forcing a new window.
fields.context: It wrongly forces session goto --resume (new window) or --force.
fields.analysis:
## Repro
In a tmux pane already bound to (working) E-1644, from the worktree:

    $ endless session resume E-1644 --db main
    Error: This pane is working E-1644. `session resume` execs in place, so it would replace that session.
      Open the target in a NEW window instead:
          endless session goto E-1644 --resume
      Or pass --force to replace this pane.

## Problem
`session resume` execs in place, so the guard refuses when the pane already has a task
variable assigned — to avoid clobbering a DIFFERENT live session in that pane. But when the
resume TARGET is the SAME task the pane already owns, there is no other session to protect:
resuming yourself replaces nothing meaningful (it is a re-enter of the task you are already on).
The guard should short-circuit that case instead of forcing `session goto --resume` (a new
window) or `--force`.

## Expected
When the pane's bound task == the resume target, `session resume <id>` proceeds without
`--force` — either a friendly no-op ("already here") or a clean re-enter/resume of the current
task. The replace-guard should fire ONLY when the pane's current task differs from the target.

## Fix location (starting point)
The `session resume` command's ownership/replace guard — the check that prints
"This pane is working E-<id>. `session resume` execs in place, so it would replace that
session." Add an equality short-circuit: if the current pane's bound task == the requested
target, bypass the "would replace that session" refusal. Confirm `session goto` and the
`--force` path stay unaffected.

## Verify
From a pane bound to task X: `endless session resume X` exits 0 (no `--force`) and does NOT
print the replace refusal; `endless session resume Y` (Y != X) still refuses without `--force`.

## Encountered
Hit live in session 6e7f46fb (the E-1644 worktree) on 2026-06-29 while trying to resume this
very task after it was completed.

## From the description

Resume execs in place to avoid clobbering a different session, but self-resuming the pane current task clobbers nothing.

Expected: same-task self-resume proceeds without --force.
